stem: Sukhmani Sahib, the "psalm of peace" of twenty-four ashtpadis in Raag Gauri of the Guru Granth Sahib, was composed by which Guru?
options: Guru Nanak Dev
Guru Ram Das
Guru Arjan Dev
Guru Tegh Bahadur
why: Sukhmani Sahib (Gauri Sukhmani, Mahala 5, ang 262–296) is Guru Arjan Dev's; its last salok calls it the jewel of peace, the ambrosial Name.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Gauri Sukhmani M5, ang 262–296

es.stem: Sukhmani Sahib, el "salmo de la paz" de veinticuatro ashtpadis en el Raag Gauri del Guru Granth Sahib, fue compuesto por ¿qué Gurú?
options: Gurú Nanak Dev
Gurú Ram Das
Gurú Arjan Dev
Gurú Tegh Bahadur
es.why: Sukhmani Sahib (Gauri Sukhmani, Mahala 5, ang 262–296) es de Gurú Arjan Dev; su último salok lo llama la joya de la paz, el Nombre ambrosial.

stem: A salok in Asa di Var (ang 469) says "dukh daaroo sukh rog": pain has become the medicine and pleasure the disease. According to the same salok, why is pleasure called a disease?
options: pleasure is a punishment for past wrongs
in comfort a person stops longing for the Lord
every kind of enjoyment slowly weakens the body
only those who seek suffering are accepted
why: Asa di Var, ang 469: pleasure is the disease because where there is pleasure, there is no longing for the Lord. The line does not praise suffering or ask anyone to seek it.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Asa di Var, salok M1, ang 469

es.stem: Un salok del Asa di Var (ang 469) dice "dukh daaroo sukh rog": el dolor se volvió la medicina y el placer la enfermedad. Según ese mismo salok, ¿por qué al placer se le llama enfermedad?
options: el placer es un castigo por faltas pasadas
en la comodidad uno deja de anhelar al Señor
todo disfrute va dañando poco a poco el cuerpo
solo se acepta a quien busca el sufrimiento
es.why: Asa di Var, ang 469: el placer es la enfermedad porque donde hay placer no hay anhelo del Señor. El verso no alaba el sufrimiento ni pide buscarlo.

stem: In a salok of Asa di Var (ang 471), Guru Nanak asks for a janeu, a sacred thread, with compassion as its cotton, contentment its thread, restraint its knot and truth its twist. What point does the salok make?
options: a cotton thread must be renewed yearly to stay pure
only those who have taken amrit may wear such a thread
a thread takes effect only once a priest has blessed it
the true thread is made of virtues and never breaks
why: Asa di Var, ang 471: such a thread of the soul does not break, get dirty, burn or wear out; the salok asks for an inner thread of virtues rather than a cotton one.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Asa di Var, salok M1, ang 471

es.stem: En un salok del Asa di Var (ang 471), Gurú Nanak pide un janeu, un hilo sagrado, con la compasión como algodón, el contento como hilo, la templanza como nudo y la verdad como torsión. ¿Qué enseña el salok?
options: el hilo de algodón debe renovarse cada año para ser puro
solo quien ha tomado amrit puede usar un hilo así
el hilo solo surte efecto si un sacerdote lo bendice
el hilo verdadero está hecho de virtudes y no se rompe
es.why: Asa di Var, ang 471: ese hilo del alma no se rompe, no se ensucia, no se quema ni se gasta; el salok pide un hilo interior de virtudes en lugar de uno de algodón.

stem: Which raag section of the Guru Granth Sahib holds hymns by Guru Tegh Bahadur and by no other Guru or saint?
options: Raag Jaijavanti
Raag Gauri
Raag Sorath
Raag Dhanasri
why: Jaijavanti, the last raag section of the Guru Granth Sahib (ang 1352–1353), has four shabads, all by Guru Tegh Bahadur; Gauri, Sorath and Dhanasri hold hymns by several Gurus.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Jaijavanti M9, ang 1352–1353

es.stem: ¿Qué sección de raag del Guru Granth Sahib contiene himnos de Gurú Tegh Bahadur y de ningún otro Gurú ni santo?
options: Raag Jaijavanti
Raag Gauri
Raag Sorath
Raag Dhanasri
es.why: Jaijavanti, la última sección de raag del Guru Granth Sahib (ang 1352–1353), tiene cuatro shabads, todos de Gurú Tegh Bahadur; Gauri, Sorath y Dhanasri contienen himnos de varios Gurús.

stem: Guru Tegh Bahadur's salok "jag rachnaa sabh jhooth hai" (ang 1429) calls the created world jhooth, often translated "false." How does the couplet itself explain the word?
options: it is a trick and does not really exist
it does not stay, like a wall of sand
it is evil and should be fled for the forest
it was made by a power lesser than God
why: Salok M9, ang 1429: "thir naa rahai jio baaloo bheet": the world does not stay steady, like a wall of sand. Jhooth here means passing, not a lie.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Salok M9, ang 1429

es.stem: El salok de Gurú Tegh Bahadur "jag rachnaa sabh jhooth hai" (ang 1429) llama jhooth al mundo creado, palabra que suele traducirse como "falso". ¿Cómo explica la palabra el propio dístico?
options: es un engaño y en realidad no existe
no permanece, como un muro de arena
es malo y hay que huir de él al bosque
lo hizo un poder menor que el de Dios
es.why: Salok M9, ang 1429: "thir naa rahai jio baaloo bheet": el mundo no se mantiene firme, como un muro de arena. Aquí jhooth significa pasajero, no mentira.

stem: A manager refuses to intimidate the people who work under her, and also refuses to be intimidated into wrongdoing by a powerful client. Which line of Guru Tegh Bahadur's saloks (ang 1427–1429) does she most closely live out?
options: one frightens no one and fears no one
the Name is the boat across the world's ocean
praise and blame, gold and iron are alike
whatever is born must perish in time
why: Salok M9, ang 1427: "bhai kaahoo kau det neh neh bhai maanat aan": the wise one gives fear to no one and accepts fear from no one. Sikhs see it lived out in his own martyrdom.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Salok M9, ang 1427

es.stem: Una gerente se niega a intimidar a quienes trabajan con ella, y también se niega a dejarse intimidar por un cliente poderoso para hacer algo indebido. ¿Qué verso de los saloks de Gurú Tegh Bahadur (ang 1427–1429) vive más de cerca?
options: no asustar a nadie ni temer a nadie
el Nombre es la barca para cruzar el océano
alabanza y culpa, oro y hierro, son iguales
todo lo que nace ha de perecer un día
es.why: Salok M9, ang 1427: "bhai kaahoo kau det neh neh bhai maanat aan": el sabio no da miedo a nadie ni acepta miedo de nadie. Los sijs lo ven vivido en su propio martirio.

stem: In Raag Dhanasri (ang 684), Guru Tegh Bahadur asks "kaahe re ban khojan jaaee": why go searching in the forest? What answer does the hymn give?
why: The One who dwells in all is with you, like fragrance in a flower or a reflection in a mirror, so search within your own heart; without knowing yourself, the moss of doubt is not cleared. Dhanasri M9, ang 684.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Dhanasri M9, ang 684

rubric.point: Says God dwells within, in one's own heart and in everyone, always present. 'God is everywhere' without saying within counts as partly.
Draws the conclusion: search within one's own self instead of leaving home for the forest; renouncing the world is not needed.
Mentions an image or line of the hymn: fragrance in a flower, a reflection in a mirror, or that without knowing oneself doubt is not removed (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el Raag Dhanasri (ang 684), Gurú Tegh Bahadur pregunta "kaahe re ban khojan jaaee": ¿por qué ir a buscar al bosque? ¿Qué respuesta da el himno?
es.why: El Uno que habita en todo está contigo, como la fragancia en la flor o el reflejo en el espejo; por eso busca dentro de tu propio corazón; sin conocerte a ti mismo, no se quita el musgo de la duda. Dhanasri M9, ang 684.

stem: Near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib (ang 1429), salok 53 says strength has slipped away and bonds have fallen, and only the Lord is refuge. What does the next salok, 54, say in answer?
why: Salok 54, ang 1429: strength has come, the bonds are broken, everything is possible; Nanak, all is in Your hands, You alone are the helper. Many Sikhs follow the tradition that it is the young Gobind's reply to his father; others read it as the ninth Guru's own answer, and the text does not settle it.

rubric.point: Says strength has returned and the bonds are broken, or that everything becomes possible.
Says this too rests with the Lord: all is in God's hands, God is the helper. Only 'strength came back' with no mention of God counts as partly.

Mentions that many Sikhs hear it as the young Gobind's (later Guru Gobind Singh's) reply to his father, or that some read it as the ninth Guru's own answer (optional, strengthens; either reading counts).

es.stem: Cerca del final del Guru Granth Sahib (ang 1429), el salok 53 dice que la fuerza se ha ido y que han caído las ataduras, y que solo el Señor es refugio. ¿Qué dice en respuesta el salok siguiente, el 54?
es.why: Salok 54, ang 1429: la fuerza ha vuelto, las ataduras se rompieron, todo es posible; Nanak, todo está en Tus manos, solo Tú eres quien ayuda. Muchos sijs siguen la tradición de que es la respuesta del joven Gobind a su padre; otros lo leen como la propia respuesta del noveno Gurú, y el texto no lo resuelve.
